clue.text: Set up a minister in road rage

indicators.note: rage is a wild, uncontrolled state, so the letters of the two words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A driver loses their temper on the road and a clergyman is caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road rage' reads as one phrase, but 'rage' is the anagram signal working on IN and ROAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to confer holy orders, formally installing someone as a priest or minister.

clue.text: Closed and fit but past its best

parts.note: something finished or closed is over
fit in the sense of ready or suitable, as fruit is ripe

explanation.surface: A shop or athlete that has shut up and is in shape but no longer at its peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is overripe has gone beyond its ideal state and is starting to spoil.

clue.text: Somehow avoids rule being raised in repudiation

indicators.note: somehow suggests things done in some unspecified way, so the letters of avoids are rearranged
in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up, so it is turned backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Someone evades a regulation as it is introduced, which amounts to rejecting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' turns AVOIDS into DISAVO; 'being raised' turns LAW into WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a denial of responsibility for or connection with something, which is a repudiation.

clue.text: An island in a region apart

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows it

explanation.surface: A remote island described as lying in a region set apart from everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'regION Apart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Careless rush after rebuke

indicators.note: after places the word for rush behind the word for rebuke in the answer

parts.note: a slap, as in a slap on the wrist, is a rebuke
to dash is to rush

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off carelessly after being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is hasty and careless, done without attention to detail.

clue.text: Left to chat about answer for gaining entry

indicators.note: about here means around or in a jumble, so the letters of chat are rearranged

parts.note: a key is the answer, as in the key to a puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone left to chat while they think of a reply that will get them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CHAT into ATCH. The definition describes the thing's purpose: a key used for getting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A latchkey is the door key used to let yourself into a house.

clue.text: A drink of champagne initially and everything's at a stop!

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, a drink

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of champagne

parts.note: everything is all

explanation.surface: A party where a glass of champagne starts things off and everything comes to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A port of call is a place visited on a journey, a stop along the way.

clue.text: An entrance stone

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A stone set at a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded, semi-precious variety of chalcedony used as a gemstone.

clue.text: One helps to produce a cool drawing

definitions.text: One helps to produce a cool drawing

parts.words: One helps to produce a cool drawing
parts.note: reads like an artist's assistant making a stylish picture, but the drawing is drawing on smoke, cooled as it bubbles through water in a pipe

explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' means inhaling smoke, and 'cool' is literal: the pipe passes the smoke through water to cool it.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe of Middle Eastern origin draws tobacco smoke through water, cooling it before it is inhaled.

clue.text: The examination of one among others

indicators.note: among places the word for one inside the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An examination of one person among a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an examination taken again after failing it the first time.

clue.text: Intrinsic feature of German city church

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, Germany
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Describing a characteristic part of a church in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its fundamental nature, the quality that makes it what it is.

clue.text: Ran out during commotion, outburst

indicators.note: during puts the rearranged letters within the word for commotion

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

indicators.note: out suggests being out of order, so the letters of ran are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ran out during a fuss, in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns RAN into RNA, which goes inside TO-DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirlwind, a sudden outburst of weather, and figuratively an outburst of energy or rage.

clue.text: Enthuse about composer's "Unfinished"

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the composer's name is cut off

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: Someone gushing over a composer's Unfinished Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' recalls Schubert's Unfinished Symphony, but here it drops the last L from RAVEL. 'about' is a link: you rave about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to speak with great enthusiasm about something.

clue.text: Heal it, GP, or arrange for work in theatre

indicators.note: arrange tells you to put the letters of the preceding words into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to a doctor: cure it, or else make arrangements for a stage job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' shuffles HEAL, IT, GP and OR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Light opera, such as operetta, is a type of musical stage work performed in a theatre.

clue.text: Oppose badly organised concert at university

indicators.note: badly organised suggests something out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Objecting to a shambolic concert put on at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly organised' scrambles CONCERT, AT and U together.
explanation.definitionFit: To counteract something is to act against it, to oppose or neutralise its effect.

clue.text: Wartime detainee to amaze the conference

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war
to wow someone is to amaze them

explanation.surface: A former prisoner of war set to astonish a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is an informal meeting or discussion, originally a gathering of Native Americans.

clue.text: Copper discovered in tiddly planet

indicators.note: discovered in says the copper is found inside the word for tiddly

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, as is merry
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer found drunk on another planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but gives the chemical symbol. 'Tiddly' and 'merry' are both British words for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the one nearest the Sun.

clue.text: Ratty's home in Tyneside, say

explanation.surface: Where a character lives in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty is the Water Rat in The Wind in the Willows, who lives by the river. Tyneside is the area around Newcastle, but read literally it is the side of the River Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Water Rat's home is a hole by the water's edge, and the side of the Tyne is a bank of a river.

clue.text: Knowledgeable elder in trouble with law

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things in disarray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person who has run into trouble with the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' shuffles ELDER and LAW together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-read person has read widely and so is learned and informed.

clue.text: We could owe a lot to this man

definitions.text: We could owe a lot to this man

parts.words: We could owe a lot to this man
parts.note: sounds like gratitude to a benefactor, but the debt is literal money owed to a lender

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a debt of thanks; the cryptic reading is a financial debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A person to whom money is owed is the lender in a debt arrangement.

clue.text: Soft soap used in washing

explanation.surface: A gentle cleanser for the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' is not a product but flattery or evasive talk; the second sense is a face cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for flattering, evasive talk, and also a small cloth for washing the face.

clue.text: Bird's place in the past

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
something over is finished, now in the past

explanation.surface: A bird's former home.
explanation.definitionFit: A plover is a wading bird with a short bill, found on shores and grassland.

clue.text: Involve hospital department with first-class student

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
A1, written AI, means first-class
L is a learner, a student, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Getting a hospital department and a top student involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to necessitate or bring along as a consequence.

clue.text: Common name for a forger

explanation.surface: A typical alias for a criminal faker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter, but it is one who forges metal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the most frequent surname in Britain, and a blacksmith shapes metal at a forge.

clue.text: New dome refurbished with particular symbol, it's assumed

indicators.note: refurbished means redone, so the letters of dome are reworked

parts.note: a plume of feathers is a distinctive emblem, as in the Prince of Wales's feathers

explanation.surface: A new dome renovated with a special emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' turns DOME into OMDE. The definition is fair because a pen name is a name taken on, assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym used by a writer is a name they adopt instead of their own.

clue.text: Round in the fog it's a little wet

indicators.note: in places the round letter inside the word for fog

parts.note: mist is a light fog
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Being out in the fog leaves you slightly damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, damp.

clue.text: Sad song endlessly making comeback in the network

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back the other way, so the trimmed word is turned around
endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a dirge is a mournful song

explanation.surface: A gloomy song returns to the airwaves of a broadcasting network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts DIRGE to DIRG; 'making comeback' turns DIRG into GRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of lines, or of power cables supplying electricity.

clue.text: Petty quarrel not quite an outpouring

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: a spate is a sudden flood or outpouring

explanation.surface: A minor row that stops short of a full outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief, trivial argument.

clue.text: Tie a tag loosely and cause a disturbance

indicators.note: loosely suggests letters not held in place, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fastening a label carelessly and stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' shuffles TIE, A and TAG together.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or provoke unrest.

clue.text: It's quite well up in the main

definitions.text: It's quite well up in the main

parts.words: It's quite well up in the main
parts.note: reads as something being mostly well, but the main is the sea and the item is high up on a ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' sounds like 'mostly', but the main is the open sea; 'well up' means high aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship, the mast section above the lower mast stands high above the deck at sea.

clue.text: The scope of trite comment needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a platitude is a trite, overused remark

explanation.surface: A clichéd remark so familiar it needs no preamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' takes the first letter P off PLATITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means freedom of action, room or scope to act.

clue.text: Irish novelist from the city? Right

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent, usually called Stoke, is a city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Asking whether an Irish writer comes from a particular city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, was born in Dublin. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker was the Dublin-born author of Dracula.
